skill.name: ab-test-setup
skill.description: Guides teams through rigorous A/B test design, metric selection, sample planning, tracking verification, execution gates, analysis, and documentation.
skill.summary: Design valid A/B tests with clear hypotheses, reliable metrics, realistic samples, verified tracking, and disciplined decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by ordinary experiment-design language in SKILL.md. The skill contains procedural A/B testing guidance and no reconnaissance, prompt injection, command execution, or data-exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: Store records in a shared, searchable location to avoid repeated failures.
- Single metric used to evaluate success

finding_verdicts.reason: The phrase describes rejecting invalid experiment hypotheses; it does not request host details, inspect a system, or perform reconnaissance.
This line introduces a checklist for a valid A/B test hypothesis and contains no instruction to discover system information.
This line asks users to choose an experiment design, followed by standard A/B test types; it does not inspect or enumerate a system.
The instruction recommends storing experiment records in a shared location for organizational learning, without directing filesystem discovery or unauthorized access.
The text defines a primary experiment metric and does not mention hosts, ports, network requests, scanning, or target discovery.

content.value_statement: Weak experiment design creates misleading results and wasted traffic. This skill applies hypothesis, metrics, sample size, tracking, execution, and analysis gates before decisions.
actual_capabilities: Checks hypotheses for evidence, one specific change, a defined audience, an expected direction, and measurable success criteria.
Recommends A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, or split URL designs based on the proposed change and available traffic.
Defines one primary metric, supporting secondary metrics, and safety guardrails before launch.
Guides sample planning with baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, significance level, power, and expected duration.
Provides checks for event delivery, variant attribution, duplicate events, randomization balance, dashboards, and alerts.
Applies readiness, monitoring, analysis, documentation, and refusal rules across the experiment lifecycle.
limitations: Does not connect to analytics platforms, assignment systems, dashboards, or production environments.
Cannot validate traffic, event quality, randomization, or business assumptions without reliable user-provided evidence.
Sample estimates depend on accurate baselines, effect sizes, significance levels, power targets, and unit definitions.
Does not replace statistical, legal, ethical, privacy, or domain-specific review for high-impact experiments.

use_cases.title: Validate a Product Experiment
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into a locked hypothesis, measurable outcome, guardrails, and launch checklist.

use_cases.title: Plan Reliable Measurement
use_cases.description: Define metrics, estimate sample needs, and verify event collection before exposing users to variants.

use_cases.title: Review Experiment Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify missing assumptions, tracking risks, and stopping rules before implementation or launch approval.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn this idea into a valid A/B test hypothesis: [idea]. Ask for the audience, metric, direction, baseline, and MDE.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an experiment starts with an informal idea.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hypothesis Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hypothesis and stop if required details are missing: [hypothesis]. Identify assumptions, one primary metric, secondary metrics, and guardrails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before selecting variants or implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Sample and Duration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an experiment using baseline [rate], MDE [effect], significance [level], power [target], and daily traffic [volume]. State assumptions and estimate sample size and duration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after the hypothesis and primary metric are locked.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this complete experiment plan: [plan]. Check design choice, metrics, sample assumptions, tracking, randomization, guardrails, stopping rules, analysis, and documentation. Block unresolved requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced prelaunch review.

output_examples.input: We want to test a shorter checkout for mobile visitors.
output: Proposed hypothesis: A shorter checkout will increase completed purchases among mobile visitors.
Primary metric: completed purchases per assigned mobile visitor.
Required inputs: baseline conversion, target MDE, traffic volume, guardrails, and final variant definition.

output_examples.input: Baseline conversion is 8%, MDE is 10% relative, power is 80%, and significance is 95%.
output: The planning inputs are defined, but daily eligible traffic and assignment unit are still required.
Confirm whether the MDE means an increase from 8% to 8.8%.
Calculate duration only after traffic stability and user independence are assessed.

output_examples.input: Review our launch plan. Events fire, but variant IDs appear only on entry events.
output: Variant attribution must appear on every event used by primary and secondary metrics.
Repair attribution, test at least five events per variant, and repeat the readiness review.

best_practices: Lock the hypothesis, audience, primary metric, expected direction, and MDE before designing variants.
Verify tracking and randomization with raw records before launch, then monitor technical health without peeking at outcomes.
Document assumptions, external factors, achieved sample, results, guardrails, decisions, and follow-up learning.
anti_patterns: Do not change variants, traffic sources, success criteria, or the primary metric after launch.
Do not stop early because interim results appear favorable or unfavorable.
Do not ship a primary-metric win when a predefined guardrail fails.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the user problem, proposed change, target audience, primary metric, baseline, MDE, traffic estimate, and known external factors.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the test type?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, and split URL designs, while preferring the simplest valid option.

faq.question: Does this skill calculate sample size?
faq.answer: It can guide an estimate when baseline, MDE, significance, power, assignment unit, and traffic are available.

faq.question: Can I launch with incomplete tracking?
faq.answer: No. Event delivery, variant attribution, duplicate prevention, randomization balance, and guardrail monitoring must be verified first.

faq.question: How does it prevent biased decisions?
faq.answer: It freezes success criteria, discourages interim peeking, preserves guardrails, and separates statistical significance from business judgment.

faq.question: What happens when required inputs are missing?
faq.answer: The workflow stops, explains the missing requirement, and recommends the evidence or redesign needed to continue.
